issues.description: Function 'setup_env': the problem statement (problem_statement.md) instructs students to call setup_env() with no parameters. The template (template_repository/helloWorld.asm) does not declare or call setup_env (no 'extern setup_env' or any call is present). The solution (solution_repository/helloWorld.asm) declares 'extern setup_env' and calls it with one argument (push 1; call setup_env). This mismatch leaves students uncertain whether they must call setup_env at all, and if so whether to pass an argument, which can lead to incorrect example code or assembly/linking/calling-convention confusion.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the artifacts on a single, clear signature for setup_env. Preferred fix (preserves the problem text): update the solution to call setup_env with no arguments (remove the 'push 1' before the call) and ensure both template and solution declare the symbol by adding 'extern setup_env' to the template (e.g., add 'extern setup_env' after 'extern printf'). Alternatively, if the function truly requires one parameter, update the problem statement to document the required parameter and update the template to include 'extern setup_env' and an example call. Ensure the example in the solution matches the documented signature.

issues.description: The register identifier for the same concept is inconsistent: the problem statement instructs students to change the misspelled register 'ecc' to 'ecx', the template file contains the invalid identifier 'ecc' (add eax, ecc) which causes compilation to fail, and the solution uses the correct register 'ecx' (add eax, ecx). Students cannot reliably map the instruction in the problem statement to a valid starter implementation because the template contains a typo for the register name and that typo blocks compilation.
issues.suggestedFix: In template/helloWorld.asm, replace the invalid identifier 'ecc' with the correct register name 'ecx' on the instruction line (change 'add eax, ecc' to 'add eax, ecx') so the template, problem description, and solution consistently reference the same register and the code compiles.
